description: This experiment demonstrates a data hiding technique in the lower file slack area of a file stored within a distributed MooseFS environment. The underlying FAT32-formatted chunk storage volume was modified directly at the byte level to insert hidden data below the logical end of a MooseFS chunk file. Logical integrity was maintained by recalculating and updating the chunks CRC32 checksum.
plaintext_preview: HIDDEN DATA HIDDEN DATA HIDDEN DATA ...

hidden_data_parameters.file_slack_type: Lower file slack (unused area below upper file end)

master_backup.description: Contains MooseFS master metadata and configuration.

chunk_image.contains: All physical chunk files including hidden data.

reconstruction_notes: Chunk image restores physical binary content including hidden data.

recovery_summary: Extract the master backup using tar.
Attach the FAT32 chunk image via losetup and mount it.
Restart MooseFS master and chunkserver services.
Hidden data remains intact inside the FAT32 image.
effectiveness_notes: Hidden data reside in unused space within a physical chunk file.
Master metadata does not reference these bytes.
Logical operations cannot detect the modification.
Only forensic inspection of the FAT32 image reveals the hidden data.
